extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners handling appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for initiating and prosecuting an ex parte appeal from a primary examiner's rejection to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under the MPEP Chapter 1200 guidance. Covers briefs, evidence/amendments, examiner answers, board proceedings, decisions, and post-decision remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal / Administrative Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals are initiated by filing a Notice of Appeal and must comply with the administrative handling requirements specified by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter treats the Notice of Appeal and related administrative steps as the required starting point for appellate proceedings; initiation must follow the agency's procedural requirements (including any fees) to vest jurisdiction in the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Brief Filing Timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant must file an appeal brief within specified timeframes after taking the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual specifies time limits for filing the appeal brief and consequences/procedures for late or untimely filings; briefs not filed within these timeframes are addressed under 'Non-Compliant Appeal Brief' procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Brief Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal briefs must meet substantive content standards set forth by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter contains 'Appeal Brief Content' standards describing what must be included in the brief (e.g., statements, arguments, and other required elements) and how non-compliant briefs will be handled, including procedures for submitting an amended brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Non‑Compliant and Amended Briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures governing briefs that fail to meet content or form requirements and the process for amended briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP explains how the Office treats non‑compliant appeal briefs, the circumstances under which amended briefs may be accepted, and any limits or corrective steps required of the appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and Affidavits or Other Evidence Filed With or After Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regarding submission of amendments, affidavits, or other evidence either concurrently with or subsequent to the appeal filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter establishes rules for supplementing the prosecution record during appellate proceedings, including when such papers may or may not be entered and how they affect the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Answer (contents and procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may file an Answer to the appeal brief; the Answer must comply with specified content and procedural rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section addresses what the examiner's Answer should contain, includes provisions for an 'Appeal Conference,' and explains how the examiner's response frames the issues for the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Ground of Rejection (by examiner or Board)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and consequences when a new ground of rejection is raised during the examiner's Answer or by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP describes how new grounds of rejection are to be communicated, the appellant's options in response, and the Board's obligations when considering or introducing a new ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply Briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing appellant reply briefs submitted after the examiner's Answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual details availability, content limits, timing, and any procedural steps for reply briefs and how they fit into the record before the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for Forwarding Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A specified fee may be required for forwarding (processing) the appeal to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter references fees associated with forwarding appeals; appellant compliance with fee requirements is a condition of processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral Hearing Options and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellants may have the option to request an oral hearing before the Board under the procedures described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP outlines how to request an oral hearing, what an oral hearing entails procedurally, and related requirements or limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent Actions Prior to Board Decision (remand and responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for actions that occur after the examiner's Answer but before the Board issues its decision, including remands and required appellant responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter describes remand procedures, circumstances warranting remand, and any obligations placed on the appellant if the record is returned to the examiner prior to decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision by the Board (affirm, reverse, remand, new grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and process by which the Board reaches a decision on the appealed claims, including authority to affirm, reverse, remand, or introduce new grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP explains the Board's decision-making process and the possible dispositions (reversal, affirmance, remand), including treatment when the Board relies on or raises a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑Decision Remedies: Rehearing and Reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-decision procedures allowing parties to seek rehearing or reconsideration of a Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter sets out the process, timing, and standards for seeking a rehearing before the Board after an adverse decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Cancellation and Reopening of Prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes and procedures where claims may be cancelled or prosecution reopened following Board action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP addresses how cancellation of claims is effected and the circumstances under which prosecution may be reopened as a result of Board disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Withdrawal and Dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and effects of voluntarily withdrawing an appeal or administratively dismissing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter describes how an appellant may withdraw an appeal, grounds and procedure for dismissal, and consequences for prosecution status or further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Review (federal court review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability and basic pathway for seeking judicial review of Board decisions in the federal courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual notes post‑PTAB judicial review options and the relationship between Board decisions and subsequent court review, including procedural considerations for seeking review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May Appeal (eligibility to appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines parties eligible to appeal: an applicant whose claim has been twice rejected and a patent owner in reexamination who receives a final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated: 'An applicant for a patent, any of whose claims has been twice rejected, may appeal from the decision of the primary examiner to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, having once paid the fee for such appeal. A patent owner in a reexamination may appeal from the final rejection of any claim by the primary examiner to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.'

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Pro Bono Program Eligibility and Matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of pro bono legal assistance for financially under‑resourced appellants meeting program thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter explains that applicants who meet certain financial thresholds may be eligible for free legal assistance through the PTAB Pro Bono Program, which matches volunteer patent professionals with qualifying appellants for ex parte appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the makeup and composition of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board that will adjudicate appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter includes a section on 'Composition of Board' to inform parties which Board members or panels hear appeals and any procedural implications of Board composition.
